verdict.root_cause: Frontend's errors are all gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE at the connect step against a single peer, 172.18.0.19:9555, the ad service's gRPC endpoint [tr_ca960af99ea5]. Ad served normally until 12:47:40, then executed an orderly server shutdown at 12:47:52 and logged nothing afterwards, with no restart in-window [tr_9b0e0b1abb98]. One second later, at 12:47:53, platform-automation applied an image-reference update on ad — the latest of 15 set/revert oscillations over ~3.2 hours [tr_be45184f233b]. The rollout stopped the running ad pod and no replacement listener ever bound 9555, so callers get connection-refused and later host-unreachable [tr_ca960af99ea5]. The deployed artifact state on ad yields no serving process; frontend's visible errors are the downstream echo.
verdict.reasoning: Frontend has no change record [tr_252b3a8e2a94], a flat error ratio [tr_5ae9ff4a4b3b], and no error-bearing or ad-touching spans in its sample [tr_301f0494f76d] — the failing calls never create a downstream span because no connection is established. Frontend's log pins the failure to one IP:port at connect, excluding DNS, timeouts and multi-backend degradation [tr_ca960af99ea5]. Ad's clean externally-initiated teardown at 12:47:52 followed by silence [tr_9b0e0b1abb98] matches the 12:47:53 image rollout [tr_be45184f233b], and ad's metrics show flat errors with far more zero-traffic intervals [tr_594655c96ff3] — a service absent, not sick. Connection-refused rules out dependency_latency and process_freeze; the fix is to pin ad to an image reference that actually starts and binds 9555.
open_questions: No dispatch verified that 172.18.0.19:9555 is the ad pod; attribution rests on port convention and timing.
Unsettled whether the hotfix image fails to start or the automation leaves the reference empty so nothing is scheduled — no pod lifecycle, image-pull or restart-count evidence was gathered.
frontend-proxy alerted simultaneously but was never queried, and five other blast-radius services were never dispatched on.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad pod was stopped and never rescheduled, leaving its port unbound regardless of which image was referenced.
alternatives.why_not: A freeze keeps the socket accepting and hangs callers; frontend sees connection-refused then host-unreachable, meaning nothing is listening and the address is gone [tr_ca960af99ea5].

alternatives.root_cause: The automation's image reference oscillation left ad pointed at an empty/invalid value, which is itself the wrong configuration.
alternatives.why_not: An image reference is the running-artifact selector, so a wrong one is bad_deploy; no non-image config entries appear in ad's change log [tr_be45184f233b].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed. Nothing changes: frontend should continue to log gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE against 172.18.0.19:9555 at the same continuous rate seen at 12:55:22-12:55:26 [tr_ca960af99ea5], and ad should continue to emit no log lines after its 12:47:52 orderly shutdown [tr_9b0e0b1abb98], until either the automation's next oscillation re-applies an image or a human stops the loop. If ad spontaneously starts logging request handling again within ~10-20 minutes, that is the oscillation cycle, not a fix.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if a dispatch confirms (a) 172.18.0.19:9555 is in fact the ad pod rather than inferred from port convention, and (b) pod-lifecycle / image-pull / restart-count evidence shows the hotfix.2 image was pulled and crash-looped or was never scheduled. Either of those settles which of rollback_image or restart_service actually addresses the mechanism, and the proposal should be re-made. It is also wrong if change history is re-read and shows a concrete non-empty prior image tag for ad immediately before 12:47:53, since the recorded prior value here is 'None' [tr_be45184f233b].
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that ad stays down and ad-slot requests from frontend keep failing for the duration of the deliberation; this is bounded because ad carries sparse traffic and frontend's aggregate error ratio is not in sustained departure from baseline. The risk of the alternative, acting now, is larger: rollback_image on ad would restore the image reference recorded immediately before 12:47:53, and that recorded prior value is 'None' [tr_be45184f233b] — the rollback would deploy ad with no image reference and guarantee no listener on 9555, converting a possibly self-healing oscillation into a definite outage. The same evidence explicitly rules out the premise that a newly shipped build is the trigger, since the identical tag was set and reverted 15 times over ~3.2 hours. restart_service is also excluded: its precondition requires the evidence to point at process state rather than a change, and here the shutdown at 12:47:52 is immediately followed by an automation-applied image update at 12:47:53 [tr_9b0e0b1abb98, tr_be45184f233b] — a change, not a process fault — and any recreated container would be torn down again by the next oscillation within 10-20 minutes. The actual fix, halting the platform-automation set/revert loop, is not in this system's action list.
proposal.blast_radius: No one, because nothing is changed. Had rollback_image or restart_service been proposed, the target would be ad alone; frontend is the named inbound caller and would see its existing gRPC connect failures continue or briefly change shape during container recreation, and frontend-proxy — which alerted simultaneously and was never queried — would be the second observer. cart, checkout, product-catalog, product-reviews and recommendation are in the blast radius but were never dispatched on and have no evidenced edge to ad.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts hitting both the frontend and its proxy simultaneously affect the full user-facing path and cannot be dismissed. No open incident covers it, and the simultaneous onset could be a frontend fault or an upstream dependency, so no fault class is favored yet.
